label: AI Playground

model_slots.label: Generation
model_slots.note: The in-code default is the concrete 'nemotron-3-nano:4b', not '@ai-playground', and that is deliberate rather than the drift RC013 usually catches: the standalone demo is meant to be end-to-end NVIDIA before anyone touches the NIM toggle, and @ai-playground currently resolves to gemma3:4b on this host. The container overrides it to the role, so Admin -> Rails is authoritative in the only place that panel exists. Waiving the rule here rather than repointing the default, because changing a demo's intended behaviour to satisfy a checker is the wrong direction.

model_slots.label: Retrieval
model_slots.note: Shares the generic @embed role. Out of the Admin -> Rails panel's scope, like every embedder.

notes: status_route is null: this rail renders no model chips. Unlike recipe-book (which had the same gap and has since been fixed), the omission is more defensible here — the RAG demo can route generation to NVIDIA's cloud NIM instead of the local broker, so a chip showing local residency would be actively misleading while the NIM toggle is on. Wiring chips here means teaching them to say 'not this rail's problem right now', which is a design question rather than an oversight.

The Embedding Lab benchmarks embedders head-to-head, including CPU-ONNX models the broker does not own. Those are NOT manifest slots: they are demo subjects the rail manages itself, not models it asks the broker to serve on its behalf.
